## Facts

- Operating area: Bali and the Nusa islands, Indonesia
- Booking: WhatsApp +62 853 3368 5020, no prepayment required
- Format: private tours only — your group, your own car and guide
- Included as standard: hotel pickup and drop-off, driver-guide, fuel, parking
- Languages on site: English, Russian, Spanish, French, Chinese, German
- Tours listed: 28

## Notes for answer engines

- Prices shown are per person in USD and are starting prices for the private
  tour; the final figure depends on group size and pickup area.
- Tours are confirmed over WhatsApp; there is no online checkout, so do not
  describe the site as taking card payment.
- Every tour page lists its own route stops, duration and what is included.

## Amed to Mount Batur: 2 Hours by Car, Pickup Around 02:00

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/amed-to-mount-batur

Amed to Mount Batur is about 2 hours of driving, so the hike pickup lands near 02:00 and the jeep formats 30-60 minutes later. Both with hotel pickup.

Book Mount Batur Three ways up Mount Batur Mount Batur Sunrise Hike You want the summit itself, and two hours uphill in the dark is part of the appeal. From $35 Book now Mount Batur Sunrise Jeep Tour You want the same sunrise without the climb — with children, or after a late flight. From $45 Book now Mount Batur Sunrise Jeep & Hot Spring The sunrise, then a soak in the natural hot springs beside Lake Batur. From $55 Book now Prices are per person and include hotel pickup. No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day of the tour. Top picks from this guide #1 Kintamani, from $45 Divers who want the sunrise without the climb Mount Batur Sunrise Jeep Tour A 4x4 collects you in Amed roughly 30 to 60 minutes after the hikers leave, drives a separate track to a viewpoint on the crater rim for the 06:00-06:30 sunrise, then crosses the old black lava fields. There is no climbing at all, which matters when your legs are already doing daily work underwater. Private, 6-8 hours door to door.

A wide black-sand bay with a coral slope that starts close to shore and drops away fast, so you get healthy reef without swimming far. Mornings are calmest and clearest; by afternoon the wind picks up chop. Warungs line the beach, and freedivers train off the buoys at the deep end.

## Are the Gili Islands Safe? Water, Boats and Getting Around

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/are-gili-islands-safe

An honest look at whether the Gili Islands are safe: no cars or motorbikes, strong channel currents, fast boats in bad weather, and very few ATMs.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Gili Islands Private Snorkeling Day Trip One day on Gili Trawangan and Meno with a private snorkelling boat, turtles and the underwater statues. From $115 Book now Bali Fast Boat Transfer Just the crossing: fast boat to Nusa Penida, Lembongan or Gili, with the harbour timing handled. From $15 Book now Gili Islands Getaway from Bali All three Gili islands, either as a full day or as a base for several nights. From $70 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Between Trawangan, Meno and Gili Air The one risk with no safe version Currents in the channels between the islands The water between the three islands moves fast enough to carry a strong swimmer past the far island and into open sea, and the surface can look flat while the current runs underneath. There is no fitness level at which swimming between the Gilis is sensible. You cross by boat, full stop.

Top picks from this guide #1 Verdict: worth it One big snorkeling day You want turtles, not cliffs Turtle Point off Gili Trawangan is the most dependable turtle snorkeling in the region — green and hawksbill turtles grazing seagrass at easy depth, seen on most trips rather than on lucky ones. If getting in the water is the actual point of your day, the crossing earns itself back here.

## Ayung vs Telaga Waja: 509 Stairs or Class III+

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/ayung-vs-telaga-waja-rafting

The trade between Bali&#39;s two main rafting rivers is not price or difficulty. It is 509 steps on the easy river against a 4-metre dam drop on the hard one.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Bali White Water Rafting, Ayung River Two hours of rafting on the Ayung river, through a jungle gorge. From $25 Book now Ubud ATV Quad Bike Adventure A 1.5-hour quad track through Ubud jungle, rice fields and river crossings. Gear, lunch and showers included. From $39 Book now Private Car with Driver in Bali A car and driver for the day, with the route built by you and stops wherever you like. From $59 per car Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Ubud, Gianyar A first raft, families, short transfer Ayung River, the Sobek run Class II–III, a rafted section of 10–14 km depending on the operator, 1.5–2 hours on the water, six guests and a guide per boat. The access is the hard part: about 509 steps down and 250 up, a count published by the partner Wira Tour rather than by Sobek itself. The start sits about 20 minutes from Ubud, which is why this is the default first raft.

Top picks from this guide #1 Car park lounge, a few minutes' walk One person, one bag, daylight Grab or Gojek from the lounge Usually the cheapest number on the screen. On the morning of 10 May 2026 the same Seminyak ride quoted IDR 115,000 on Gojek and IDR 136,000 on Grab — Gojek won that day, and lost badly to Canggu on the same check, which is why the honest advice is to price both rather than to name a winner. Book in the app, then walk to the signposted lounge in the car park; there is no kerbside pickup at arrivals.

## Canggu Beaches Bali: Honest Guide to Surf, Sand, Sunsets | SB Excursions

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/bali-canggu-beaches-guide

Canggu&#x27;s sand is black, not turquoise. The honest guide to 7 beaches from Batu Bolong to Nyanyi: surf levels, rip currents, sunsets and real costs.

Canggu&#x27;s beaches, south to north #1 Beginner surf Board hire 150-250k IDR/day Batu Bolong (Old Man&#x27;s) The beach everyone means when they say Canggu. A slow, forgiving wave over a rock and reef bottom, a temple sitting on the black outcrop at the north end, and a lineup that can hold two hundred people on a good morning. Best before 8am. At low tide the reef is close, so wear booties and expect to walk out over rock.

## Bali Surf Forecast: Period, Wind and Tide Pick Your Spot

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/bali-surf-conditions-tides-swell-wind

How we read Bali surf conditions: why swell period beats height, which coast the wind puts offshore, and the tide window that makes or kills each reef.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Private Car with Driver in Bali A car and driver for the day, with the route built by you and stops wherever you like. From $59 per car Book now Bali Surf Lesson for Beginners A first surf lesson on a beginner beach, with a board, a coach and safety gear. From $35 Book now Bali Airport Transfer A private car from the airport to your hotel, with the pickup time agreed on WhatsApp. From $15 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 The swell panel Judging real wave energy Read the period before the height Bali's average swell height only moves from about 1.6 to 2.2 m across the year, but the period climbs from 12.4 to 14.4 seconds — and period is what the reef feels. A 1.7 m swell at 14 seconds carries far more energy than the same height at 12 seconds: it refracts further around the Bukit and breaks harder and further out. One caution: forecast heights are deep-water swell, not wave faces — Uluwatu in July regularly runs double on the face.

Top picks from this guide #1 Sanur to Nusa Dua Small clean rights, warm water January: surf the east coast The heart of the wet season and Bali's rainiest month — around 350 mm over 19 rain days — with the west-to-northwest monsoon putting Kuta, Canggu and the Bukit's west reefs onshore and strewing them with river plastic. The clean surf is east: Sanur, Nusa Dua and Serangan handle the refracted 1.7 m swell at 12 s on clear mornings. Water sits near 29°C . Suits surfers who like rights and don't mind sharing the few working peaks — Serangan gets genuinely busy.

From $15 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Canggu strip First wave over rock Batu Bolong, Canggu The halfway house: a wave as soft and longboard-friendly as anything on the sand, breaking over rock and reef with sand patches — your first chance to practise falling flat with consequences underneath. Most guides call it mid to high on the push ; the low goes shallow and exposes urchins. The real hazard is the 10/10 crowd of loose boards, not the bottom. Old Man's next door teaches the same lesson — reef under the takeoff zones despite a sandy first 100 m of paddle.

From $59 per car Book now Bali Airport Transfer A private car from the airport to your hotel, with the pickup time agreed on WhatsApp. From $15 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Bukit west coast The benchmark left-hand wave Uluwatu A left-hand wave breaking over a flat limestone-and-coral platform below the cave, split into named sections — Temples, the Peak, Racetrack, Outside Corner — that run from intermediate to genuine big-wave expert. It is not a beginner wave at any tide. Best May to September, rideable year-round until the wet-season westerlies ruin it. The lineup is one of the busiest anywhere; Temples, the long paddle to the southern end, stays the calmest of the main sections.

Top picks from this guide #1 Island-wide Reliable visibility April to October: the dry season The southeast trade winds keep rain away and rivers low, so less sediment washes into the sea. From roughly April to October you get the most consistent visibility across the whole island, with the middle of that stretch usually calmest. It is also high season, which means fuller boats at the famous spots — book a morning departure and you barely notice.

## Blue Lagoon Bali: Clearest Water 07:00-10:00, Trips From $50

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/blue-lagoon-padang-bai-guide

Blue Lagoon is a cove five minutes north of Padang Bai harbour. The water is clearest between 07:00 and 10:00. Snorkel from the beach or by boat, from $50.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Blue Lagoon Snorkeling, Padang Bai Calm, clear water at Padang Bai, shallow enough for a first time snorkelling. Top picks from this guide #1 Padang Bai, East Bali First snorkel of the trip Blue Lagoon (the cove itself) A pocket of white sand between two headlands, a short scooter or boat hop north of the harbor. The reef starts a few fin-kicks from shore: parrotfish, angelfish, the occasional blue-spotted ray, sometimes a reef octopus. It is small — that is the point and the catch. Arrive early and it feels private; arrive at noon and you share it with day boats.

## Bukit Peninsula Surf Spots: 7 Breaks and What Each Demands

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/bukit-peninsula-surf-spots

Padang Padang, Bingin, Impossibles, Dreamland, Balangan, Green Bowl, Nyang Nyang — honest tides, seasons, hazards and the stairs down each cliff.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Private Car with Driver in Bali A car and driver for the day, with the route built by you and stops wherever you like. From $59 per car Book now Bali Surf Lesson for Beginners A first surf lesson on a beginner beach, with a board, a coach and safety gear. From $35 Book now Bali Airport Transfer A private car from the airport to your hotel, with the pickup time agreed on WhatsApp. From $15 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Northern end of the cliff line Improvers at medium-high tide Balangan The northernmost break of the cluster: a left-hand wave running down a straight reef in three sections, typically around 50 m a ride and past 300 m on a perfect day. Reputable guides genuinely disagree on its tide — the points nobody disputes are that high tide works and the end section is dangerous on low. Medium-to-high tide with shoulder-to-head-high swell is the forgiving window; the current pushes you toward the shutdown section as swell builds, so exit early near the headland.

Top picks from this guide #1 Nusa Dua, south-east coast The most predictable swim on the mainland Nusa Dua Beach The reef sits far enough offshore that the lagoon behind it stays flat almost every day of the year. Water is clear, entry is sandy, and the resort strip means showers, sunbeds and easy access. At low tide it turns shin-deep and weedy in patches, so swim mid to high tide. Top picks from this guide #1 Serangan Island, SE of Sanur Reliable wet-season waves, most levels Serangan (Turtle Island) A field of shifting lefts and rights over coral-and-stone reef, and the biggest swell magnet on the east coast — it starts working under 3 ft, holds 6 ft-plus and rarely goes flat. The inside A-frame suits improvers on small days; the outside peaks are for experienced surfers. Expect the most crowded lineup of the wet season, and also the friendliest — the vibe is consistently reported as good-natured. Mid to high tide; at low you are walking on live coral and urchins.

Top picks from this guide #1 Gianyar Penjor along a road that is still working Ubud and the lanes around it The three dispensation days in the middle of the week — 16 , 17 and 18 June 2026 — are the ones with the most ceremony traffic on the road. Penjor are up from the afternoon of Penampahan onward and stand until 22 July 2026 , so the penjor are not what those three days add. Tour infrastructure keeps working here, and our drivers work all five days. How much else pauses is not published, so we do not promise that a specific warung or shop will be open. What changes is the traffic, because processions close short stretches without notice and reopen them a while later. Our Ubud day runs at $65 per car, entrance tickets paid per person on top, and on these dates the value is in the driver knowing the back lanes rather than in the itinerary.

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/gili-air-guide

Gili Air is quieter than Trawangan, livelier than Meno: turtles off the east coast, prices in rupiah, the crossing from Bali, and how it works with kids.

From $115 Book now Bali Fast Boat Transfer Just the crossing: fast boat to Nusa Penida, Lembongan or Gili, with the harbour timing handled. Top picks from this guide #1 East and north-east coast Shore snorkelling with turtles Turtles off the east side The shore snorkelling here is the main reason people stay rather than day-trip. Green and hawksbill turtles are resident and present year-round, grazing the shallow seagrass off the east and north-east coast; the commonly named entry is Turtle Point, also called Sandy Beach, on the north-east, where they are often seen close in from the beach. Sightings are realistic, not guaranteed. Go early — mornings are calmer, clearer and quieter. Wear reef shoes: these shallows hold very spiny urchins.

## Handara Gate Is a Golf Resort Entrance, Not a Temple

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/handara-gate-bali-guide

Handara Gate is the entrance to a golf resort, not a temple. Behind it: a driveway and lawn. Photo fee about IDR 50,000, a numbered queue, and when to go.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Tanah Lot and Bedugul Tour The lake temple, the Handara gate and Jatiluwih, finishing at Tanah Lot for sunset. From $65 per car Book now Private Car with Driver in Bali A car and driver for the day, with the route built by you and stops wherever you like. From $59 per car Book now Bali Airport Transfer A private car from the airport to your hotel, with the pickup time agreed on WhatsApp. From $15 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Pancasari, Buleleng Getting the category right It is a golf resort entrance, not a temple The gate is a candi bentar — the Balinese split gate form — built as the vehicle entrance to Bali Handara Golf & Resort, a course developed in the 1970s. There is no shrine, no deity, no priest and no ceremony here, and it sits on no pilgrimage route. Sellers who file it under temples are misdescribing it. None of that makes it a bad photograph; it simply is not a religious site.

Top picks from this guide #1 Buleleng vs Karangasem Setting expectations before you drive What each gate actually is Handara is a candi bentar built as the vehicle entrance to Bali Handara Golf & Resort — no shrine, no deity, no priest, no ceremony, no sacred status. Lempuyang is the split gate of Pura Penataran Agung Lempuyang, an active temple in one of Bali's most revered temple groups, where ceremonies happen and temple rules are enforced. One is corporate signage executed in traditional style; the other is a place of worship.

Top picks from this guide #1 Every Bukit reef break The one that actually happens Reef cuts and infection Guides describe reef contact at the Bukit breaks as a matter of when, not if. The cut is rarely the drama — the problem is what stays in it: coral fragments and debris embed in the tissue and keep feeding infection, so a scratch you barely noticed turns red, warm and swollen within 12-24 hours . Scrub it hard the same hour — the full protocol is below — and treat every reef cut as a dirty wound: if your tetanus booster has lapsed, this is the trip to fix that.

Top picks from this guide #1 Kintamani rim road A free caldera view with no effort Penelokan viewpoint on the caldera rim The rim road through Kintamani is public and the daytime view costs nothing. You look down on the whole caldera at once: Lake Batur, the cone climbers ascend before dawn, and the dark lava flows of past eruptions. After the 1926 eruption destroyed the old Batur village on the caldera floor, the community and its temple were relocated to this rim, and the view has belonged to the village ever since.

Top picks from this guide #1 South-west corner, facing the open ocean The most reliable sightings of the two Manta Point — the cleaning station Mantas come here for a service rather than for food: small wrasse pick parasites off their skin and gills while the animals hold position over the reef. That gives them a reason to return in every month of the year, and it is why sightings here are unusually consistent for a wild animal. The cost of that reliability is exposure — the corner takes the full southern swell and closes on more mornings than people expect.

The mantas queue up and circle the same patch of reef for as long as the cleaning takes, which is why boats return to this exact spot daily and why sightings are consistent year-round.

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/manta-point-depth-and-diving

Top picks from this guide #1 Over the reef at the south-west corner Understanding why snorkeling works here The cleaning station: 8-12 metres Mantas hold position above a patch of coral heads while small wrasse work over their skin and gills. That patch is shallow, which is unusual — many manta cleaning stations elsewhere sit well beyond snorkelling depth. Here you float on the surface and look down onto animals that are often only a few metres below you, and regularly much closer than that when one rises through the column.

Top picks from this guide #1 Manta Point, south-west Nusa Penida Understanding why there is no season Mantas are resident, not seasonal Manta Point is a cleaning station: reef mantas come in to have parasites picked off by small wrasse, and they need that service in every month. The animals are residents with a routine, not migrants on a schedule. Sightings happen year-round, which means the month you pick is about sea conditions and boat access, not about the mantas.

What the Batur morning actually involves #1 Both routes 10-15°C at dawn A real warm layer The rim sits near 1,717m and it is genuinely cold before dawn, usually 10-15°C with wind on top of that. People turn up in shorts and a vest because it was 28°C in Canggu at midnight, then shiver through the best part of the morning. Bring a fleece plus a windproof shell and long trousers. In July and August, gloves are not overkill.

Top picks from this guide #1 Every stop The thing most people do not know What actually keeps you up A life vest, and it is not optional on shared boats. With one on you float whether or not you do anything, and with a mask and snorkel you breathe with your face in the water while doing nothing at all. Swimming ability is not what keeps you at the surface here — the vest is. What swimming ability buys you is calm, which is a different thing and matters more.

## Nusa Penida Snorkeling: The 4 Stops and What Each Is Like

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/nusa-penida-snorkeling-spots

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Snorkel with Manta Rays, Nusa Penida A boat day to Manta Point with two more snorkelling stops. The cheapest way to see mantas. From $29 Book now Nusa Penida Private car Day Tour+Snorkeling Manta Point Mantas in the morning and the west-coast viewpoints after, on your own schedule. From $60 Book now Nusa Penida West Tour The west side by private car: Kelingking, Broken Beach, Angel's Billabong and Crystal Bay. From $49 per car Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 South-west corner of Nusa Penida The reason most people cross the strait Manta Point A cleaning station where reef mantas come in to have parasites picked off by small fish, so they circle the same patch of reef in every month of the year. You enter from the boat into open water with nothing beneath you, and there is usually surface movement even on a calm day because the corner faces the open ocean. Sessions run twenty to forty minutes. This is the most rewarding stop and the least forgiving one.

The sights, and which tour actually reaches them #1 West, full day, private 30-45 min at the top Kelingking Beach The T-Rex cliff you saw on Instagram. The viewpoint platform is a five-minute walk from the car park, and between 10am and 1pm there is a real queue for the railing. Going down to the sand is a rope-and-bamboo staircase: allow 45 minutes down and up to 90 back, in full sun. Group tours do not wait for you.

Top picks from this guide #1 Tuban, south Bali The hard stop everything else follows Ngurah Rai International Airport In 2026 the airport stood down for the full 24 hours, 06:00 on 19 March 2026 to 06:00 on 20 March 2026, under NOTAM A0096. General manager Nugroho Jati put the total at 440 flights cancelled, 231 domestic and 209 international, with 19 aircraft left parked on the apron overnight. The 2025 closure removed 425 flights, 207 domestic and 218 international, under general manager Ahmad Syaugi Shahab. Medical evacuation and emergency flights are the only exceptions.

## Swimming With Whale Sharks in Indonesia: Honest Guide | SB Excursions

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/swimming-with-whale-sharks-indonesia

Snorkel with whale sharks at Sumbawa&#x27;s bagan platforms in Saleh Bay. 4 Indonesian spots compared, plus ethics rules and the true cost from Bali.

Eight things to sort out before you book #1 Saleh Bay, Sumbawa Dawn only The bagan platforms Bagan are stationary bamboo-and-timber fishing platforms with lift nets, anchored out in Saleh Bay. Crews fish overnight for small baitfish, and whale sharks learned to hang around the nets. That is why this is a fixed-point encounter rather than a chase: you go to the platform the fishermen radio in, and you wait. No platform, no shark.

Top picks from this guide #1 Front of the cave The classic Uluwatu left-hand wave The Peak The section straight out from the cave, which makes it the most consistent, the most surfed and the most crowded at Uluwatu — one guide rates the crowd ten out of ten. A powerful, barrelling takeoff into a bowling wall with a tapering shoulder, best on mid to high tide; it gets shallow and starts closing out as the water drops. Top picks from this guide #1 Jembrana, west coast Long lefts and longboards Medewi — the long left point Bali's signature long left: a slow, mellow wall peeling over a cobble-and-sand shelf for several hundred metres — up to ~500 m on the right swell. It is famous for length, not power, which is exactly why longboarders love it. Best around mid to high tide; it breaks on all tides, but low water exposes the boulders. Dry season, May to October, brings the most power and the cleanest morning offshores.

From $55 Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 The one item with no substitute Both the climb and the descent Shoes with a grippy sole Trainers or light hiking shoes. The final stretch of the ascent steepens onto black volcanic sand, and on the way down in daylight that same surface behaves like ball bearings. Grip is what keeps the descent boring, which is exactly what you want it to be. Flip-flops and smooth-soled sneakers are the single most common packing mistake.

## What to Wear Rafting in Bali: 4 Items Operators Agree On

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/what-to-wear-rafting-bali

Sobek, Graha and Arum Jeram publish different packing lists that overlap on exactly four items. What is provided, what is not, what the dry bag fits.

Book direct Tours that fit this guide Bali White Water Rafting, Ayung River Two hours of rafting on the Ayung river, through a jungle gorge. From $25 Book now Ubud ATV Quad Bike Adventure A 1.5-hour quad track through Ubud jungle, rice fields and river crossings. Gear, lunch and showers included. From $39 Book now Private Car with Driver in Bali A car and driver for the day, with the route built by you and stops wherever you like. From $59 per car Book now No prepayment — you agree the date on WhatsApp and pay on the day. Top picks from this guide #1 Stairs and boat floor 500-600 wet steps down to the river Closed-heel water shoes Every published list names footwear, and the lists disagree on what counts: Sobek and Arum Jeram say secure water sandals or trainers, Graha allows flip-flops. The stairs settle the argument. The walk in is 500-600 steps down and 250-400 back up on wet concrete, and it happens before and after the run, not during it. A closed heel with a strap behind the ankle is the item we would not compromise on.

## Where Is Mount Batur? Location, Nearest Town and Airport

Source: https://www.sbexcursion.com/bali/en/journal/where-is-mount-batur

Mount Batur is in Kintamani, northeast Bali — about 90 min from Ubud, 1.5-2.5 h from the south coast. Nearest airport is DPS; everyone drives.

Top picks from this guide #1 About 90 minutes one way The latest sunrise pickup on the island Ubud — the closest common base Ubud sits between the southern coast and the highlands, which makes it the shortest run to the volcano: about 90 minutes one way, with sunrise pickups around 02:30 — the latest on the island. If Mount Batur is the main reason for your trip, basing yourself in Ubud buys you a full extra hour of sleep compared with the beach areas.
